stories.title: Evolution towards higher unitary conductance in mammals makes BK channels more efficient and precise
stories.description: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. Mammalian BK channels are distinguished by an exceptionally high unitary conductance (~250 pS), while invertebrates exhibit a significantly lower unitary conductance. We confirmed the evolutionary trend to high unitary conductance and used computational models to examine how differences in unitary conductance affect calcium activation of BK channels and influence neuronal dynamics. We show that mammalian BK channels are activated more efficiently by calcium and generate stronger repolarizing currents than lower unitary conductance channels. Channels with lower unitary conductance require greater channel density in the cell membrane, leading to stronger competition for calcium and reduced activation. In contrast, high unitary conductance channels minimize competition, enabling more effective activation and repolarization. Incorporating these channel properties into a neuronal model revealed that mammalian-type BK channels enhance spike-timing precision, consistent with the evolution of fine motor control and advanced neuronal processing in mammals.

stories.title: The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf stabilized three adjacent ice sheets during the last glacial period
stories.description: Global ice volume peaked between ~26,500 and 19,000 years ago and resulted in the Laurentide, Innuitian and Greenland ice sheets coalescing in Baffin Bay, a semi-enclosed basin between Greenland and Canada. However, the configuration of their marine terminating margins, which help establish the boundary conditions and sensitivity to processes that govern ice-sheet retreat, remains unclear. Here we compile bathymetric data and report a geomorphic study of the Baffin Bay continental slope. We provide evidence for slope-grounded ice during the last glacial interval and trace its maximum depth imprint around most of Baffin Bay. We interpret ice-contact features to have resulted from a basin-spanning ice shelf that was ~1,400–2,100 m thick, once corrected for relative sea level. The extensive ice shelf (150,000 km2), supported by the basin geometry, buttressed, mechanically coupled, and promoted thickening of the adjacent ice sheets. Informed by sediment cores, we infer that ice-shelf collapse triggered rapid ice-sheet retreat, linking abrupt Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet instability to embayment-scale ice-shelf dynamics. The Baffin Bay Ice Shelf shows that ice-shelf loss can rapidly reorganize marine ice sheets, an analogue for how weakening buttresses may accelerate future Antarctica ice-stream retreat. An enormous ice shelf spanned Baffin Bay during the last glacial period, and its rapid retreat during the last deglaciation probably destabilized the surrounding ice sheets, according to an analysis of bathymetric data

stories.title: A futile Na+ K+ transport cycle augments energy expenditure in beige adipocytes
stories.description: Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1)-independent energy dissipation has been proven to serve physiological functions in beige adipocytes. Here we show that a futile sodium/potassium (Na+/K+) transport cycle is preferentially amplified in mouse and human beige adipocytes and contributes to UCP1-independent energy expenditure. In mice, cold exposure activates a sympathetic–thyroid hormone signaling axis that coordinatedly induces the Na+/K+-ATPase subunit ATP1A2 together with Na+ and K+ channels, increasing bidirectional ion flux across the plasma membrane while maintaining ionic balance. Atp1a2+Kcnk3+ adipocytes are detected in mouse inguinal white adipose tissue after cold exposure. Acute inhibition of Na+/K+-ATPase reduces energy expenditure in mouse and human beige adipocytes, whereas overexpressing Atp1a2 in murine adipocytes potentiates energy expenditure, independent of UCP1. Adipocyte-specific Atp1a2 deletion impairs thermogenic capacity and exacerbates diet-induced obesity in mice. Expression of a human ATP1A2 missense variant reduces ATP1A2-dependent respiration in mouse adipocytes. Together, these identify ion transport as a tunable ATP-consuming mechanism that expands the thermogenic repertoire of beige adipocytes. A futile Na+ K+ transport cycle, which is preferentially active in beige adipocytes, is shown to promote energy expenditure independent of uncoupling protein 1.
